title: Potentially smooth finite normalization of an affine group model
statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$ and a fixed algebraic closure $ ar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $\mathcal G=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be an affine group scheme of finite type over $A$, where $B$ is a finitely generated flat $A$-algebra [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Group schemes over a ring have multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with that ring as base. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Suppose $\mathcal G_K$ is smooth and geometrically connected. There is an injective local map $A	o R$ to a henselian discrete valuation ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], whose residue field is identified with $ ar k$ compatibly with $k	o ar k$. Put $L=\operatorname{Frac}R$ and $B_R=B\otimes_A R$. Let $C$ be the integral closure of $B_R$ in $B_R\otimes_R L$, namely the subring of elements satisfying a monic polynomial with coefficients in $B_R$. Then $C$ is a finite $B_R$-module, and $\mathcal N=\operatorname{Spec}C$ has a smooth affine finite-type $R$-group-scheme structure such that $
u:\mathcal N	o\mathcal G_R$ is a group homomorphism and $
u_L$ is an isomorphism. The special fibre $\mathcal N_{ ar k}$ is a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over $ ar k$. Both $
u$ and its special-fibre map $
u_{ ar k}:\mathcal N_{ ar k}	o\mathcal G_{ ar k}$ are finite and surjective on underlying spaces; finite means that the source coordinate ring is a finite module over the target coordinate ring. No excellence assumption on $A$ is imposed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0405381: Section 3.3, Proposition 3.4 and Corollary A.4, with Theorem A.6; local-extension reductions at the beginning of Section 5 and following Lemma A.9, printed pp.5-6,9,27-30

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-extension-given-residue-field] to $A$ and the specified extension $\bar k/k$, obtaining a flat local algebra $S$ with maximal ideal $\pi S$ and residue field the specified $\bar k$. Multiplication by $\pi$ on $S$ is injective: tensor the injection $A\xrightarrow{\pi}A$ with the flat module $S$. Apply [lem-sfb-principal-regular-local-completion-dvr] to obtain the complete DVR $D=\varprojlim S/\pi^nS$, with uniformizer the image of $\pi$ and residue field $\bar k$. The composite $A\to D$ is injective and local. Indeed a nonzero $a\in A$ is $u\pi^n$ with $u$ a unit, whose image is nonzero in the domain $D$; units remain units, and $\pi$ lies in the maximal ideal. The residue identification is compatible with the original $k\to\bar k$.

source.place: Tag 03C3, lemma-flat-local-given-residue-field; Tag 0328, completion step with a general uniformizer

proof.text: Put $F=\operatorname{Frac}D$ and $E=B\otimes_A D$. It is finitely generated over $D$ by the images of generators of $B$ and is flat: for a $D$-module $M$, $M\otimes_D E=M\otimes_A B$, so injections are preserved. Its generic fibre is $\mathcal G_K\times_K F$, hence smooth. For clarity, smooth base extension and products here follow directly from the lifting definition of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: a map out of a tensor product is a pair of maps with the specified common scalar map, and their lifts give its lift; presentations base change by the same generators and relations. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal] to this smooth generic fibre and then [lem-sfb-raynaud-faltings-normalized-reduction] to $E/D$. Obtain its finite extension $L/F$ and the stated integral-closure algebra $C$ over $R$, the integral closure of $D$ in $L$.

source.place: Appendix Theorem A.2, geometrically normal generic fibre case; Corollary A.4, proof before constructing the group law

proof.text: The DVR $D$ is Noetherian, and by Step 1 it is complete for its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata] it is a Nagata ring; for the prime $(0)$ this says that the domain $D$ itself is N-2, so the integral closure $R$ of $D$ in the finite extension $L/F$ is a finite $D$-module. As a subring of $L$, $R$ is a domain, so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] it is a Noetherian local ring, complete for its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, and $\mathfrak m_R$ is the only prime of $R$ contracting to $\mathfrak m_D$. By [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-local-dvr], which imposes no separability on $L/F$, $L$ is the fraction field of $R$ and there is a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $R$ over $\mathfrak m_D$ such that $R_{\mathfrak q}$ is a DVR whose maximal ideal contracts to $\mathfrak m_D$. Uniqueness gives $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_R$; as $R$ is local, its elements outside $\mathfrak m_R$ are units, so $R=R_{\mathfrak m_R}$ is a complete DVR with fraction field $L$, finite over $D$, and $D\to R$ is local. Its residue field is a finite extension of the specified $\bar k$: reduce a finite set of $D$-module generators modulo the maximal ideal of $R$. Since $\bar k$ is algebraically closed, the induced embedding of $\bar k$ onto that residue field is an isomorphism. This fixes the required identification. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian], $R$ is henselian. The composite $A\to R$ is the required injective local map. Since $B_R=E\otimes_D R$, the algebra $C$ of Step 2 is exactly the integral closure prescribed by the item, and Step 2 supplies its finiteness, flatness, normality and generic isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 032W (lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata), Tag 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local) and Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr): the integral closure of a complete DVR in a finite extension is a finite complete DVR; completion and prescribed algebraically closed residue field as in Prasad--Yu Appendix Remark A.1 and Corollary A.4

proof.text: Write $P=C\otimes_R C$. This is flat over $R$, since tensoring an injection first with one flat factor and then with the other remains injective. Its generic fibre is the coordinate algebra of $\mathcal G_L\times_L\mathcal G_L$, which is smooth by the tensor lifting argument in Step 2 and normal by [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal]. Its special fibre is reduced: apply [lem-sfb-flat-geometrically-reduced-pullback] over $\bar k$ with both factors $\operatorname{Spec}(C/\mathfrak m_RC)$, which are geometrically reduced by Step 2 and locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], since they are finite type over a field; flatness over the field holds for every vector space. Thus [lem-sfb-dvr-normal-generic-reduced-special] applies both to $P$ and to $C$. In each case every element of its generic algebra integral over the original algebra lies in that original algebra.

source.place: Corollary A.4, proof: normality of the product of the normalization with itself, using Remark A.3

proof.text: Let $\Delta_L$, $\iota_L$ and $\epsilon_L$ be multiplication, inverse and identity on the generic coordinate algebra $C_L=B_R\otimes_R L$. For $c\in C$, choose a monic relation $c^n+b_{n-1}c^{n-1}+\cdots+b_0=0$ with $b_i\in B_R$. Applying $\Delta_L$ shows $\Delta_L(c)$ integral over $P$: its coefficients are the images of $\Delta_{B_R}(b_i)$ in $P$. Step 4 puts it in $P$. Applying $\iota_L$ similarly gives an element integral over $C$, hence in $C$. Applying $\epsilon_L$ gives an element of $L$ integral over $R$, since $\epsilon_{B_R}(b_i)\in R$; it lies in $R$ because a DVR is a PID and [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] says a PID is integrally closed. Restriction therefore defines $R$-algebra maps $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_R C$, $\iota:C\to C$ and $\epsilon:C\to R$. Each extends the given map on $B_R$.

source.place: Corollary A.4, proof: extending the group law by normalization; the affine monic-polynomial calculation is written out here

proof.text: The two maps in each group diagram agree after inverting a uniformizer of $R$, because there they are the group diagrams of $\mathcal G_L$. They already agree over $R$: the targets $R$, $C$, $C\otimes_R C$, and $C\otimes_R C\otimes_R C$ are flat over $R$ and thus embed in their localizations (multiplication by every power of the uniformizer is injective). Equality after localization is consequently equality on every element. These maps give $\mathcal N=\operatorname{Spec}C$ a group structure, and compatibility on $B_R$ says precisely that $\nu$ is a homomorphism. Its generic fibre is the isomorphism in Step 2.

source.place: Corollary A.4, proof: compatibility with the generic group law; verification of all group diagrams by flatness

proof.text: The special fibre is a finite-type geometrically reduced group over $\bar k$, so [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] makes it smooth. The generic fibre is smooth as well. Since $C$ is a flat finite-type algebra over the Noetherian ring $R$, it has a finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. By [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], these two smooth fibres make $\mathcal N\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ smooth. It is affine and finite type by construction. This proves every asserted property of the special-fibre group.

source.place: Corollary A.4, proof: geometrically reduced group fibres imply smoothness

proof.text: The inclusion $B_R\subset C$ is injective and integral by its definition, so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] proves that $\nu$ is surjective on underlying spaces. For a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $B_R/\mathfrak m_RB_R$, lift it to a prime of $B_R$ containing $\mathfrak m_RB_R$. Lying-over gives a prime of $C$ contracting to that prime; it contains $\mathfrak m_RC$, so it gives a point above $\mathfrak p$ in the special fibre. This proves special-fibre surjectivity without assuming injectivity on the quotient rings. The finite set of $B_R$-module generators of $C$ maps to generators of $C/\mathfrak m_RC$ over $B_R/\mathfrak m_RB_R$, proving finiteness of the special-fibre map. Finiteness of $\nu$ was Step 2. No hypothesis on excellence of the original $A$ was used: the auxiliary complete $D$ was constructed in Step 1.

source.place: Section 3.3 (going-up); Corollary A.4; finiteness and surjectivity after reduction
